question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=3x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $\pi /18$ | $\pi /9$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\pi /6$ | $\pi /3$ |

Using the above, we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /18}^{\pi /9}3{sec}^{2}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}3{sec}^{2}⁡(u)\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(u)\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
